name: Taiwanese nationalism
summary: Taiwanese nationalism holds that the people of Taiwan form a nation with its own identity, history and culture, distinct from China, and that Taiwan is a sovereign state not subordinate to the People's Republic of China. It is civic and multi-ethnic in its mainstream form, tied to democratization against KMT one-party rule, and combines support for self-determination by referendum with cautious, status-quo-preserving practice.
scope: The mainstream pan-green strand as expressed in the Democratic Progressive Party's resolutions (1999 Resolution on Taiwan's Future, 2004 Resolution on Ethnic Diversity and National Unity, 2007 Resolution on Normalization of Taiwan as a Nation, 2023-era status quo statements) and associated Taiwanization policies. It excludes Hoklo ethno-nationalism and the ROC-centred Chinese nationalism of the KMT; the party's non-nationalist social and economic policies are used only as inferred, low-confidence answers.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The DPP resolutions call for a social security system protecting dignity, and the nationalist camp defends the national health insurance as a point of civic pride.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 2001 resolution commits the DPP to protect the minimum wage and amend labor law, though it favors gradual rises over a substantial jump.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The same resolution seeks a free market economy with less irrational state intervention yet also managed liberalization; nationalism itself is neutral on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: The DPP resolutions stress liberalization and a market mechanism, so broad public ownership is not part of the program; inferred from the economic resolution.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Resolutions call for a fair and efficient tax system and fiscal balance, with no strong stance on higher wealth taxes; adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: The 2001 resolution endorses well-organized unions and orderly collective bargaining as a route to labor protection.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nationalism as such has no doctrine on property rights; the DPP texts emphasize both market liberalization and social justice, so adherents split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The resolutions call for clear oversight of mergers and acquisitions and transparency, and 2011 criticizes privatizing profits while socializing pollution; inferred, not central.

cut-welfare.rationale: The DPP resolutions propose building social security for the unemployed and reforming pensions to ensure dignity, the opposite of cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: No nationalist or DPP text proposes worker ownership; collective bargaining is the stated labor model, so this is inferred as disagreement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents prize democratic rights won against the KMT White Terror, but also back counter-infiltration security; inferred lean against broad surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The DPP is socially liberal but has not pushed recreational legalization; inferred modest disagreement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The 2004 ethnic diversity resolution opposes ethnic blame and for coexistence, but speech restriction is not addressed; adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: Taiwanese nationalism is bound up with democratization against one-party strongman rule, so bypassing gridlock via a strong leader is distrusted.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalists seek a sovereign normal state with its own constitution and defense, so calling the state unnecessary contradicts the core project.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is not a nationalist issue; Taiwan already restricts firearms strictly and the progressive DPP does not contest this.

empower-police-military.rationale: The 2011 and 2019 resolutions call for self-defense capability and defense autonomy, though police authority is not a theme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The party is socially liberal in general, but sex work is an unresolved issue within the DPP; no stated nationalist position.

decide-locally.rationale: The nationalist project centers on the unitary state of Taiwan acting as one sovereign people, though the DPP supports administrative decentralization.

rehabilitation.rationale: Progressive human rights framing implies support for rehabilitation, but this is not documented as a nationalist position.

traditional-family.rationale: The DPP backs marriage equality and the nationalist camp is socially liberal; inferred from party positions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The 2019 resolution celebrates the constitutionally protected Marriage Equality Act; the pan-green camp enacted it though some adherents dissent.

abortion-legal.rationale: The DPP is socially liberal and Taiwan permits abortion by law; this is inferred, not a nationalist doctrine.

more-religion-public.rationale: Nationalism is civic and secular in its public claims; DPP is socially progressive, so a larger public religious role is not sought.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The 2004 resolution says the state must reflect on persecution of indigenous peoples and other ethnic groups and restore dignity to victimized communities.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Progressive DPP circles accept it but the nationalist ideology itself is silent; adherents split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Building Taiwanese identity through local cultures, native languages, and Taiwan-centric education is a stated central aim of the DPP resolutions.

gradual-change.rationale: Nationalists want a new constitution and name change yet insist on cautious, progressive steps toward China; mixed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 2004 resolution welcomes new immigrants and mainland Chinese arrivals as part of a civic nation; inferred as disagreement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1999 resolution seeks admission to the UN and other bodies, which leads adherents to favor stronger international organizations for recognition; inferred from this.

free-trade.rationale: The 1999 and 2001 resolutions endorse bilateral FTAs, WTO entry and market liberalization.

nation-first.rationale: Sovereignty and security are placed first, but the camp also seeks cooperation with democracies; the statement is read as interest-first and is contested.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The nationalist camp identifies with democracies and human rights, yet has no stated position on foreign intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Border control is implied by sovereignty and security concerns with the PRC; adherents oppose open borders, inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: The 2004 resolution ranks sustainable development above economic development, but growth limits are not endorsed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The 2019 resolution calls for green energy and coal reduction, though drastic action is not stated.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The 1999 and 2001 resolutions build the national future on a knowledge industry and a green technology island; optimism is inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The DPP sought a non-nuclear society, as its 2019 resolution reports, so expanding nuclear power is opposed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nationalists celebrate the democratization struggle but through elections; whether revolution is justified is not addressed and adherents split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Strong stress on referendum and direct civic rights implies skepticism of expert rule; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The DPP economic resolutions call for liberalization and a free market economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed by the texts; adherents split between market liberals and social democrats.

land-value-tax.rationale: The camp does not prioritize this fiscal idea; no stated position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed, only a general call for a fair tax system; adherents split.

basic-income.rationale: Not proposed in the DPP resolutions, which prefer social security and pensions tied to work; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The resolutions favor FTAs and an open trade framework, so tariffs for protection are not a stated aim.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Resolutions seek a knowledge economy led by government platforms yet oppose irrational intervention; mixed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No relevant stated position; support for SMEs is mentioned but not as a property doctrine.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labor and market economy are assumed throughout the DPP economic program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Calls for financial stability and discipline imply keeping central banking; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Collective bargaining is endorsed but not state-recognized bodies; adherents split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Taiwanese nationalism arose in opposition to one-party KMT authoritarian rule and links democratization to its success.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The nationalist project is a democratic republic with a popularly elected president; monarchy is foreign to it.

democracy-best.rationale: Democratization is described as the main motivation of Taiwanese nationalism, and democracy is part of national identity against the PRC.

direct-votes.rationale: The 1999 resolution calls for completing referendum legalization to realize direct civil rights, and a referendum on status changes.

workers-councils.rationale: Representative parliamentary democracy and direct elections are the model; councils are absent.

right-to-secede.rationale: The nationalists claim Taiwan's right to determine its status separate from the PRC, but a general right of regions to secede is not articulated as principle; read via self-determination.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equality of civic citizens and anti-authoritarianism run against rule by naturally superior people.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nationalists pursue change via elections and referendums and seek peace framework, but defend armed self-defense; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: The camp seeks peace and a stable framework while deterring the PRC; glorifying war is absent.

separate-church-state.rationale: The party is liberal and civic in orientation and the state is secular; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Civic liberal nationalism with a marriage equality record rejects scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: National security and sovereignty are state responsibilities in the DPP resolutions, and a state defense capability is called for.

military-superiority.rationale: Nationalists want to deter the PRC and boost self-defense, but superiority over rivals is unrealistic and not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Taiwanese nationalism is described as civic, multi-ethnic, and rejecting Hoklo ethno-nationalism; the 2004 resolution says Taiwanese identity is not nativism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalist historiography frames history through colonial and authoritarian rule over the Taiwanese people, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The resolutions favor social justice and opportunity and welfare floors but not equality of outcomes; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The 2004 resolution commits to indigenous identity reconstruction and recognizing wrongs; land authority specifically is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Nationalists frame Dutch, Qing, Japanese, and KMT rule as colonial but there is no documented reparations claim; split.

civilizational-union.rationale: The 1999 resolution rejects the One China principle and any union with China despite shared cultural roots.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No stated doctrine; liberal strands lean yes but social justice strands lean no.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The movement is built on human rights and civic liberties won against authoritarianism, not on duties first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental protection is endorsed but intrinsic value is not addressed.

limit-population.rationale: No such program is in the resolutions and Taiwan has a low birth rate; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The DPP resolutions embrace industry, technology and a knowledge economy.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The knowledge-industry and green technology island proposals lean pro-technology; contested on disruption.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed by any source; DPP digital policy exists but no stated position on algorithmic rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between rights and security concerns.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement is about overturning the KMT order and building a new one; restoring a lost order is not its framing.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The 1999 resolution speaks of a safe, cautious, progressive China policy, which is pragmatic, but the nationalist cause is value-driven; split.

direct-action.rationale: Nationalists emphasize electoral and referendum routes, though the Sunflower and tangwai movements used protest; inferred lean against.

means-match-ends.rationale: Democratization movement links peaceful democratic means with democratic ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The program is modern industrial and knowledge economy.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The resolutions assume specialized industrial economy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The camp supports welfare floors but not a communist principle; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: The market economy is accepted in the DPP resolutions.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The resolutions embrace business competitiveness and SMEs, so profit as exploitation is not their view.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-communism and democracy are core to the DPP and the camp.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural policy is based on market partnerships and exports, not collectivization.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The resolutions treat trade and economic reciprocity as foundations for peace.

taxation-theft.rationale: The resolutions assume tax and fiscal balance for public welfare.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal rights orientation of the DPP implies agreement; not directly documented.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The camp supports group rights to language and culture, including indigenous and Hakka, and national self-determination.

conscription.rationale: Taiwan maintains conscription for national defense and the DPP calls for strengthened self-defense; adherents accept it as security necessity.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democratic voice is central to the nationalist story; exit as a check is not emphasized.

state-as-business.rationale: The 2001 resolution proposes corporate management techniques in government, but citizens as customers is not framed that way; mixed.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social justice and welfare themes imply material conditions matter; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not stated; nationalists criticize KMT-dominated media historically but without this thesis.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The 2004 resolution rejects ethnic discrimination and promotes equal dignity of ethnic groups.

organic-representation.rationale: Direct elections and referendums are central, not family-based representation.

total-state.rationale: The movement fights a former party-state that directed culture and education.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 2007 resolution calls for becoming a normal nation, which carries some rebirth framing, but decadence is not the theme.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The 1999 resolution says Taiwan's jurisdiction lies only in Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu and affiliated islands.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not discussed; the Wikipedia article describes Taiwanese nationalism as civic and tied to democratisation, which excludes rule by personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Labor rights and humane conditions are demanded.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Taiwan-centric curricula claim to correct imposed KMT narratives, but no epistemological stance is stated.

universal-morality.rationale: The resolutions appeal to universal human rights and democratic values; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Pluralist multiculturalism and party competition are preferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no stated position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed, although Taiwanese abroad are recognized as nationals; no clear position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Taiwanization policy promotes Taiwanese Hokkien, Hakka and Formosan languages in media and schools, and a draft 2003 law would have made fourteen languages national.

school-vouchers.rationale: The DPP texts favor public education reform and not vouchers; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The 1999 and 2001 resolutions aim to eliminate fiscal deficits and achieve fiscal balance.

economic-freedom.rationale: Open free market economy is paired with democracy in the resolutions, and economic miracles are credited to sovereignty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Democratic institutions rather than moral example are preferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 1999 and 2023 resolutions say the right to self-determination belongs to the Taiwanese people.

force-without-un.rationale: The camp seeks UN membership and international legitimacy and is defensive in posture; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: None of the DPP resolutions or nationalist sources takes a position on faith versus reason, and religious Taiwanese are prominent adherents.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; the 2004 resolution welcomes new immigrants, suggesting inclusive treatment but the statement is split.

class-collaboration.rationale: The 2001 resolution seeks management-labor negotiation mechanisms rather than conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage preservation is promoted; sacrificing it is contrary to the program.

dominated-front.rationale: The camp aligns Taiwan with the US, Japan and other democracies against PRC pressure, so a front of states resisting Western powers is rejected.

workers-nation.rationale: The national community is a civic whole, not a working-class one.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The DPP is progressive with marriage equality and gender equality in policy.

ban-interest.rationale: The resolutions never mention interest; their aims to improve the financial system and diversify investment presuppose ordinary lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 2004 resolution opposes ethnic hierarchy and assimilation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement sees state as a vehicle of national self-determination and democracy.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The 2019 resolution aims for coal reduction and green energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The 2004 resolution abandons assimilation policies and favors peaceful coexistence with ethnic diversity.

elite-replacement.rationale: The 2004 resolution welcomes new immigrants and rejects blame on groups.

proportional-representation.rationale: The DPP and smaller pan-green parties have backed electoral reforms favoring smaller parties; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Nationalists seek to be a stabilizing democratic example but not to spread their government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Progressive orientation implies agreement, though not documented as nationalist doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The DPP criticized the KMT's bribery culture and party-state, and proposed an anti-corruption agency.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not discussed in the resolutions; restricting reproduction conflicts with the party's human-rights commitments.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The 2007 resolution pursues transitional justice, investigating White Terror victims and those responsible for the 228 Incident.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program includes welfare, social security, and active state economic management.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The 2004 resolution promotes ethnic coexistence and mutual acceptance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 2004 resolution stresses dignity of every ethnic group and rejects ethnic blame.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to the nationalist program.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nationalist narratives describe successive outside regimes that displaced indigenous peoples, as the 2004 resolution says; the statement is general so low confidence.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal citizenship under common law is implied, with no stated position on personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: A liberal secular orientation opposes it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of any program; contrary to Taiwanese food culture.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Secular civic framework implies this; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1999 resolution makes status changes depend on all Taiwan residents in a referendum, and rejects the PRC's unilateral claims.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; export orientation exists but no doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: The 2004 resolution condemns persecution and collective blame.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nationalists condemn PRC coercion and hold a defensive posture; the principle is inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not a doctrine; market competition is endorsed but struggle between peoples is not.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The camp cherishes free party competition after one-party rule; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The 1999 resolution frames PRC claims as coercion and insists Taiwan not be subordinate to another; inferred as consistent with non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: The resolutions pursue constitutional restructuring with a new constitution and judicial reform.

vanguard-party.rationale: The sources do not discuss vanguard parties; the idea is alien to a democratic movement built in opposition to party-state rule.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not directly addressed; social justice is stated but priority for the poor is not.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Taiwan has no council housing tradition and the DPP resolutions never discuss tenant purchase rights, so the ideology gives no direction.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The program protects labor rights and collective bargaining.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not a nationalist position and contrary to the social justice stance.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The nationalist narrative says there would be no Taiwanization without diversity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The movement is shaped by opposition to martial law and emergency rule.

party-controls-media.rationale: Lifting of media restrictions after martial law is part of the nationalist democratization story.

party-commands-army.rationale: Opposed to the KMT party-army legacy; civilian command is assumed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The 2004 resolution welcomes new immigrants but sets out no naturalization timeline, so adherents have no common position.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The sources describe party competition but not binding discipline on members, so this is a neutral placeholder rather than a stated view.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty is the movement's core demand, though shared groupings may be acceptable.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The ROC president commands forces in practice; not a stated doctrine.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance has no bearing on Taiwanese national identity politics, and no source addresses it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious rule is not addressed; the DPP's liberal, democratic orientation implies a civic, secular order.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists would defend Taiwan in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Opposed to the cultural suppression of KMT era.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Direct presidential elections with term limits are seen as safeguards.

recall-officials.rationale: The camp supports expanded direct citizen rights via referendum, and Taiwan has recall law.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The DPP favors closer ties with the US and Japan.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing markets and property are assumed; no program abolishes rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: The DPP calls for strengthening professional self-defense and conscription reform, not replacing the army with armed citizens; some civil defense emphasis.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not stated; the knowledge and technology economy is the program.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The 1999 resolution rejects the One China principle and says Taiwan and the PRC do not belong to each other; unification is the opposite of the program.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not stated; the movement drew heavily on intellectuals and professionals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The statement that Taiwan culture is not a branch of Chinese culture and the diversity resolution imply cultural parity among groups.

death-penalty.rationale: Taiwan retains capital punishment and the DPP governments carried out executions, though party human rights circles oppose it; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality education was implemented under DPP governments; inferred, not core.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A progressive science and technology oriented camp rejects it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; Taiwan law is descent-based but the 2004 resolution welcomes new immigrants and mainland-origin residents.

minority-language-support.rationale: The 2004 resolution points to adding native languages to curricula and reviving Hakka and aboriginal languages; the 2003 draft would make fourteen national languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The diversity resolution covers ethnic and cultural groups, not religious exemptions from general laws, so adherents are split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Liberal pluralism implies agreement; not documented.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; Taiwan seeks to help developing countries via trade and expertise.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sovereignty claim is political and constitutional, and the economic program is open market.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 2007 resolution proposes a new constitution, with a referendum, though not necessarily via a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Taiwanese nationalists ground the economic miracle in democracy and reject authoritarian growth bargains.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The 2001 resolution proposes helping developing countries grow their industries; inferred general duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: DPP seeks a non-nuclear society and relies on conventional self-defense with US backing; no nuclear weapons program.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1999 resolution celebrates the 1996 presidential election by popular vote as a core achievement.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The resolutions stress financial stability but do not address central bank independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalists claim only Taiwan and nearby islands and are not engaged in a land-for-peace conflict; split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; social justice themes but no doctrine.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A historical-theoretical dispute about the USSR that Taiwanese nationalist sources do not engage; adherents simply condemn Soviet-style communism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental protection and a non-nuclear aim imply precaution; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: The DPP seeks close security ties with the US and Japan and treats peace in the Taiwan Strait as regional concern.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The camp rejects the PRC's claim over Taiwan and holds that Taiwan cannot be annexed without its people's consent; inferred from the consent principle.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religion-state relations are not part of the nationalist program in the sources read, and temples and churches are both active in Taiwan.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ROC president is a partisan figure and the 1999 resolution seeks nonpartisan foreign policy consensus only.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Taiwanese nationalists reject the PRC claim of force against Taiwan and call such coercion illegitimate.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The 1999 resolution declares One Country, Two Systems fundamentally inapplicable to Taiwan.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not discussed; a sacred head of state contradicts the civic, democratic character the Wikipedia article ascribes to the movement.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The resolutions call for a fair and efficient tax system without specifying rate structure, so adherents are split.

character-from-environment.rationale: No nationalist source takes a stance on the nature-versus-nurture question, though the 2004 resolution treats identity as culturally shaped.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The movement fights the KMT party-state and demands constitutional democracy.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is absent from the resolutions, which focus on a knowledge economy and green technology on the island.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional design favors popular sovereignty; no mixed estates.

leader-cult.rationale: Taiwan's democratization era includes removing authoritarian-era leader cult symbols under transitional justice; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not discussed in any nationalist or DPP source consulted, so no direction can be inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrinal question that has no counterpart in Taiwanese nationalist thought.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not part of the program; Taiwan carried out land reform earlier under the KMT.

refugee-return.rationale: Taiwanese nationalist sources do not address return rights for refugees from conflicts, so this is left neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The 1999 resolution limits jurisdiction to Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu, abandoning ROC-era claims over China.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religion is not addressed in the sources; punishing apostasy contradicts the DPP's social-liberal rights orientation.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not discussed in any source; a dress law for women contradicts the DPP's social liberalism.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed; the resolutions do not address Taiwan joining any monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The camp rejects union based on shared ancestry or culture with China.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The 2004 resolution supports Hakka and indigenous cultural revival and local cultural institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalist history stresses regimes and identity, not modes of production; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: The 2001 resolution calls for fair competition and merger oversight; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: The 2001 resolution calls for financial stability and oversight but does not say whether failing banks should be rescued with public money.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The resolutions pursue judicial reform and constitutional order, not unlimited majority rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The DPP has gender quotas in its own candidate lists; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Trade integration and WTO entry are goals.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The 2001 resolution proposes to include labor conditions in trade regulations.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Republican civic nationalism implies this; not documented.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Taiwan-centric history and geography curricula are an established nationalist goal, with Taiwanese history taught alongside China's.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Nationalists claim colonialism harmed Taiwan and reject rule by outsiders.

patriotic-education.rationale: Taiwan-centric curricula to build a Taiwanese national identity are stated policy, though framed as civic rather than loyalty drilling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The DPP supports indigenous and ethnic-group affirmative measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: Nothing in the resolutions proposes shifting money creation to a public body, and a market financial system is assumed, so mild disagreement is inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The program accepts capitalist market economy and sees growth possible; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The nationalists oppose PRC influence abroad and do not claim a historic sphere.

delink-world-market.rationale: The program deepens trade and global integration.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not part of nationalist analysis and contrary to labor rights stress.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anti-discrimination and ethnic equality are stated.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The DPP seeks a new constitution that protects rights; entrenchment inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Taiwan nationalists dispute the Cairo and Treaty-based claim of PRC sovereignty but specific voiding is not stated.

elective-rulers.rationale: Direct elections are celebrated as the core of Taiwan's democratization.

minority-veto.rationale: Referendum and majority rule are the mechanisms stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The movement resisted KMT martial law and one-party rule as unconstitutional.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The ROC has a semi-presidential system; no stated position.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Progressive DPP policy includes animal welfare; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Same basis as the sentience statement: DPP-era animal welfare law accepts regulated use of animals, an inference rather than a stated nationalist position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The sources frame social obligation through state welfare and social justice, not through a duty of the privileged, so adherents are split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim that the nationalist sources never engage; adherents hold no common view.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian hegemony thesis absent from the sources, though nationalists describe KMT cultural dominance as imposed by force rather than consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The program uses global trade as a growth route.

native-born-offices.rationale: The 2004 resolution welcomes new immigrants as part of the nation; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Taiwan's strategy relies on trade and foreign capital and partnerships.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nationalists reject ROC territorial claims and the PRC claims; they seek no lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The 2004 resolution supports indigenous recognition but not political primacy; split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Nationalists ground the democratic order in opposing KMT authoritarianism rather than fascism as such, so adherents are split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-communist and anti-authoritarian DPP supports condemning both; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historiographic debate unrelated to Taiwanese nationalism, with no source position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Transitional justice includes removing authoritarian symbols, as in the 2007 resolution.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The DPP gender equality framework does not take a stated position on boys' and men's disadvantage, so adherents are split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources contain no position on the gender symmetry of domestic violence, and progressive DPP framing would lean against, so it is left neutral with low confidence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Taiwanese nationalists present liberal democracy as Taiwan's identity against PRC claims about Asian values.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The movement opposed KMT martial law and military party-state.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care programs are supported in the 2016 achievements, though paid domestic work is not stated.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is a general Chinese-heritage cultural norm that nationalists neither promote nor reject in the sources read.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; elections and hiring reform proposed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Open foreign capital is welcomed, but sensitive PRC investment is restricted; split.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The DPP seeks pension reform and annuity systems of public design.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional democracy and fiscal discipline are assumed; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Nationalists replaced the KMT's forced Mandarin policy and favor multilingualism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The resolutions welcome foreign capital but do not address foreign land ownership, though security concerns about PRC buyers exist, so adherents are split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law framing is not covered by the sources, and this US-specific legal doctrine has no nationalist position.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The 2004 resolution prioritizes sustainable development over economic development, but consumerism itself is never criticized.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Taiwan's posture is defensive and peaceful.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The camp treats the PRC's force against Taiwan as illegitimate and endorses nonintervention norms.

corporate-influence.rationale: The 1999 resolution criticizes KMT party business interests and bribery, but general corporate lobbying is not addressed, so adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The 2023 resolution seeks to protect democratic constitutional order from foreign infiltration, and the DPP passed a foreign infiltration act.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The DPP has implemented child-care subsidies; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property purchase limits are not discussed in the sources, so this is neutral.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; unemployment social security instead.

democratic-peace.rationale: The camp aligns with democratic partners; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The sources do not discuss a general duty to obey, but nationalists revere the rule of law and mildly disagree with the claim.

non-intervention.rationale: The camp opposes outside coercion including the PRC's claim to resolve the status unilaterally.

industrial-unions.rationale: The 2001 resolution endorses well-organized unions but says nothing about craft versus industrial structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 2004 Resolution on Ethnic Diversity says past persecution was by KMT elite cliques, not any ethnic group, so mainland immigrants should not be collectively blamed.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The DPP expanded marriage legal recognition via the Marriage Equality Act.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The 2001 resolution seeks transparency of government information.

local-production.rationale: The resolutions favor trade integration and exports, and nothing promotes localized production, though local autonomous energy and water supply is mentioned.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not addressed; parties and institutions are the vehicle.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The camp seeks UN and international law participation but guards sovereignty; split.

religious-nation.rationale: Taiwanese nationalism is civic and multi-ethnic, and not defined by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The 1999 resolution rejects PRC claims of hegemony and subordination.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The 2001 resolution calls for balanced regional finances; no clear stance.

defeat-communism.rationale: The party is anti-communist, but the 1999 resolution seeks dialogue and peace framework with China.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The DPP resolutions use government-private resource consolidation.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not applicable to this ideology; no stated position.

religion-illusion.rationale: Taiwanization and the DPP stress pluralism and religious freedom, not a view of religion as consolation; inferred from the party's social-liberal outlook.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The DPP governs a market economy and favours trade-led development; inferred from its party profile, as nationalism itself has no economic doctrine.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mainstream pan-green social liberalism seeks gender equality through law and reform, not systemic economic change; inferred from the party profile.

socialized-care.rationale: DPP social-liberal policy favours public long-term care and childcare support; inferred from its party profile, not from nationalist texts.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Taiwanization promotes Taiwanese, Hakka and indigenous languages against Mandarin-only policy, not purging foreign words; inferred from that language campaign.

treaties-binding.rationale: The 2004 resolution on ethnic diversity affirms rights of indigenous and other groups, so honouring agreements is inferred; no treaty doctrine is documented.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nothing in DPP resolutions points to common-property communities; inferred from its commitment to a market economy and individual rights.

majority-settlement.rationale: The 2004 resolution on ethnic diversity and the civic, multi-ethnic character of the nationalism reject steering the majority into minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The DPP works within a market economy with social-liberal welfare and does not seek a third system; inferred from its party profile.

missingStatements.text: The people of a self-governing territory should decide by referendum whether it unites with a larger state.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1999 resolution says any change to Taiwan's status must be decided by all residents of Taiwan by referendum.

missingStatements.text: A country should seek full membership in international organizations even if a larger neighbour objects.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1999 and 2007 resolutions call for admission to the UN, WHO and other bodies under the name Taiwan despite PRC objections.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to states whose status is disputed; the bank already has statements on international organisations and national self-determination.

notes: Taiwanese nationalism has no economic or social doctrine of its own; most non-sovereignty answers are inferred from DPP platforms and are low confidence. Huadu strands emphasize the ROC name, while Taidu strands seek a Republic of Taiwan. The practical status-quo position under Tsai Ing-wen and Lai Ching-te differs from the party charter's independence clause.
